passage: When I moved into the hostel, I thought laundry, food and cleaning would take an hour a week. By day nine my bucket was full of clothes, my mug had grown a green skin, and there was no clean shirt. Anand, my roommate, looked at the pile and said only, "So it starts." I felt astonished at how fast everything piles up when nobody does it. That weekend I made a few small rules: wash the mug the moment it is empty, wash two shirts every night, and write the shopping list on the wall when something runs out. Two weeks later, the pile was gone, and I hardly noticed the work. Imran

qa.q: How many days had passed when Imran's bucket was full of clothes?
qa.a: The bucket was full of clothes by day nine.

qa.q: What was Imran feeling when looking at the pile of clothes and the mug?
qa.a: Imran felt surprised and a little dismayed at how quickly things pile up when nobody does them.

qa.q: What small habits did Imran adopt to prevent a large weekly mess?
qa.a: Imran began washing the mug as soon as it was empty, washing two shirts every night and writing a shopping list on the wall.

qa.q: How might Anand see Imran's first week in the hostel?
qa.a: Anand, who says "So it starts", seems to have seen it all before and is amused, though not unkind.

grounding: Shows a hostel student surprised by how quickly laundry, dishes and groceries pile up, and using small daily habits.

passage: Hostel warden's note, Monday. Leela moved into the rented room two floors up two weeks ago. On day nine I passed her door and saw a tower of clothes on the bed, a cold pan on the floor and an empty grocery bag. She looked embarrassed. I did not lecture. I asked how the week was going. She shrugged and said, "Nobody told me it would pile up so fast." We sat on the step, and she wrote a plan on the back of a notebook: one plate a day, laundry every Saturday, grocery list on Sunday. This morning the room was tidy and the bed was clear. Gautam, warden

qa.q: How many weeks ago did Leela move into the rented room?
qa.a: Leela moved into the rented room two weeks ago.

qa.q: What was Leela probably feeling when Gautam saw the tower of clothes?
qa.a: Leela was probably embarrassed and surprised by how fast things had piled up, since she shrugged and said nobody had told her.

qa.q: What small step helped Leela keep the room tidy?
qa.a: Leela wrote a plan of one plate a day, laundry every Saturday and a grocery list on Sunday.

qa.q: How does Gautam see Leela's messy room?
qa.a: Gautam sees a student learning something new and treats it gently, asking how the week is going instead of lecturing.

grounding: Shows a student living away from home for the first time surprised at how quickly laundry, dishes and groceries pile up, and using small daily habits.
